req.title: Register rejects duplicate username
req.statement: The system shall render an error message when POST /auth/register is called with a username already present in the users table.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that POST /auth/register must render an error message when a duplicate username is submitted. The pre-loaded database already contains users Rahul, Anjali, Ishaan, Diya, and James. Tests cover: (1) positive — a genuinely new username registers successfully and redirects to /auth/login; (2) negative — submitting an existing username returns HTTP 200 with the exact error string 'User <name> is already registered.'; (3) boundary — registering the same username twice in sequence within one test session (first succeeds, second fails), exercising the state transition from 'user absent' to 'user present'; (4) decision-table — verifying the exact error message format including the username interpolation, catching string-mutation operators; (5) NEG — verifying that a username that differs by one character from an existing one is accepted, confirming the uniqueness check is exact-match only.

tests.name: test_register_new_user_succeeds
preconditions: Database is initialised with pre-loaded rows (Rahul, Anjali, Ishaan, Diya, James).
Username 'Vikram' does not exist in the users table.
expected: No error message in response body.
trace: R-FLASKR-006 — success path: new username must be accepted and redirect issued.
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

def test_register_new_user_succeeds():
    r = client.post('/auth/register',
                    data={'username': 'Vikram', 'password': 'cloud'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.headers['Location'] == '/auth/login'
    assert b'already registered' not in r.data

tests.name: test_register_duplicate_all_preloaded_users
preconditions: Database is initialised with pre-loaded rows containing Rahul, Anjali, Ishaan, Diya, James.
actions: POST /auth/register for each of the five pre-loaded usernames.
expected: Each response body contains the exact error string 'User <name> is already registered.' with the correct interpolated name.
trace: R-FLASKR-006 — EP: all pre-loaded users form one equivalence class of duplicates; catches mutations that hard-code a single username in the error check.
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

def test_register_duplicate_all_preloaded_users():
    users = [
        ('Rahul', 'stone'),
        ('Anjali', 'cloud'),
        ('Ishaan', 'stone'),
        ('Diya', 'cloud'),
        ('James', 'river'),
    ]
    for username, password in users:
        r = client.post('/auth/register',
                        data={'username': username, 'password': password})
        assert r.status_code == 200, f'Expected 200 for duplicate {username}'
        expected_msg = f'User {username} is already registered.'.encode()
        assert expected_msg in r.data, f'Missing error for {username}'
